messages.subject: covariances in path model
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm doing a path analysis with a set of observed variables. As a first step I made a saturated model and the I dropped my non-significant paths (p>0.1). 

My initial model was this:
ww1 <- 'ww ~ smi + ug + fdb + sex + seas
                  smi ~ sex + seas                  
                  ug ~ smi + sex + seas
                  fdb ~ smi + ug + sex + seas
                  seas ~~ 0*sex'

And my final path model looks like this:
ww3 <- 'ww ~ ug + seas
          ug ~ sex + seas
          fdb ~ ug + seas
          seas ~~ 0*sex
          ww ~~ 0*fdb'

"sex" and "seas" are two level exogenous dummy variables. I do not want the to be correlated. 
But note the last line from my final model (ww3). If I don't add that line (ww ~~ 0*fdb), lavaan automatically correlates "ww" with "fdb", although I don't want that. 
Why is he doing that? Is this the right way to handle this issue?

Thank you in advance!

Attila

On 10/01/2013 11:36 AM, F�l�p Attila wrote:
> "sex" and "seas" are two level exogenous dummy variables. I do not want
> the to be correlated.

Why? If you do a simple regression, would you force your predictors to
be uncorrelated?

It is best not to touch exogenous variables. That is why you get this
warning:

lavaan WARNING: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [sex seas];
Please use fixed.x=FALSE or leave them alone

> But note the last line from my final model (ww3). If I don't add that
> line (ww ~~ 0*fdb), lavaan automatically correlates "ww" with "fdb",
> although I don't want that.

Again, why? If you do a multivariate regression, why would you want to
force the residuals to be uncorrelated?

But if you don't like lavaan's defaults, please use the lavaan() function.

Yves.

Dear Yves,

Thank you for your answers! I'm quite new in path analysis, that's the reason I'm doing some things which might see inappropriate. 

I don't want to force my predictors to be uncorrelated, but as I learned from my lectures about path analysis (mostly from AMOS), I should trace the paths between the variables, which can be related to each other. In my case, sex and season are two variables which might influence the other endogenous variables from my model, but sex and season are not related to each other. That's the reason I didn't correlated them. But if you say, that I should, I redo the analysis in that manner. Related to the warning message, I didn't got it, because I set the fixed.x parameter to FALSE. 

Related to the second issue. My "fdb" parameter was regressed on the "ww" in the first model, but its' effect was not significant, so I removed that path from the model. That's the reason I forced the parameters to be uncorrelated in the final model. Should I leave the default settings in the final model? What do you thing?

Thank you very much for your comments! It really helps me a lot!

Best wishes,
Attila

messages.subject: Re: covariances in path model
parts:
On 10/01/2013 11:00 PM, Fülöp Attila wrote:
> I don't want to force my predictors to be uncorrelated, but as I learned
> from my lectures about path analysis (mostly from AMOS), I should trace
> the paths between the variables, which can be related to each other. In
> my case, sex and season are two variables which might influence the
> other endogenous variables from my model, but sex and season are not
> related to each other. That's the reason I didn't correlated them. But
> if you say, that I should, I redo the analysis in that manner. Related
> to the warning message, I didn't got it, because I set the fixed.x
> parameter to FALSE.
It is best not to touch the exogenous variables, and leave fixed.x to TRUE.

> Related to the second issue. My "fdb" parameter was regressed on the
> "ww" in the first model, but its' effect was not significant, so I
> removed that path from the model.

I would only remove it if there is conceptual reason to do so, not
because it happens to be not-significant.

Yves.
